Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has an article on:
аванс
Wikipedia bg

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French avance, from avancer (“to advance”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ɐˈvans]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ans
  • Syllabification(key): а‧ванс
  • Hyphenation(key): аванс

Noun

[edit]

ава́нс • (aváns) m (relational adjective ава́нсов)

  1. advance, imprest (amount of money, paid before it is due)
  2. handicap (an allowance of a certain amount of time or distance in starting, granted in a race, or other contest of skill, to the competitor possessing disadvantages; or an additional weight or other hindrance imposed upon the one possessing advantages, in order to equalize, as much as possible, the chances of success)
    Synonyms: предимство (predimstvo), преднина́ (predniná)
  3. lead (precedence; advance position; also, the measure of precedence; as, a lead of a boat’s length, or of half a second; the state of being ahead in a race)
    Synonym: преднина́ (predniná)

Kumyk

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Russian аванс (avans, “advance payment”).

Noun

[edit]

аванс • (awans)

  1. advance, advance payment (money paid before work is completed)
    аванс алмакъ ― awans almaq ― to receive an advance
    аванс бермек ― awans bermek ― to give an advance; to pay in advance

Adjective

[edit]

аванс • (awans)

  1. advance (relating to an advance payment)
    аванс отчёт ― awans otçöt ― advance report

Derived terms

[edit]
  • аванслыкъ (awanslıq)

References

[edit]
  • Бамматов, Б.Г. (2011), “аванс”, in Кумыкско-русский словарь, Махачкала

Russian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French avance.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ɐˈvans]
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)

Noun

[edit]

ава́нс • (aváns) m inan (genitive ава́нса, nominative plural ава́нсы, genitive plural ава́нсов, relational adjective ава́нсовый, diminutive ава́нсик)

  1. advance (of money), prepayment, payment on account
    Synonym: зада́ток m (zadátok)
  2. (figurative, in the plural) advances, overtures
